title: Reactivity series & extraction
examples: When we use the reactivity series, what does it tell us about metals?
Can you explain the difference between displacement and electrolysis?
Why is it sometimes better to use electrolysis instead of a chemical reaction?

explain.say: Today we look at how we get metals from ores.
A displacement reaction happens when a more reactive metal pushes another out.
For example, zinc metal can displace copper from copper sulfate solution.
Sometimes the metal is too reactive for simple displacement.

draw.text: Electrolysis needed for highly reactive metals

explain.say: Electrolysis uses electricity to force a chemical change to happen.
For instance, we use electrolysis to extract aluminium from its ore.

faq.q: Why do we need electrolysis for aluminium?
faq.a: Aluminium is very reactive, so it cannot be displaced by other metals easily. Electrolysis provides the necessary electrical energy to force the reaction.
asks: How do we get aluminium from its ore?
Is displacement enough for aluminium extraction?

faq.q: What is the difference between displacement and electrolysis?
faq.a: Displacement uses a more reactive metal to push another metal out of a solution. Electrolysis uses electricity to force the reaction when the metal is too reactive.
asks: When should I use electrolysis instead of a chemical reaction?
Does electricity always make a reaction happen?

faq.q: Can I use the reactivity series to predict reactions?
faq.a: Yes, the reactivity series shows which metals are more reactive than others. A more reactive metal will displace a less reactive metal.
asks: If I put magnesium in copper sulfate, what happens?
What does the reactivity series tell us?

faq.q: What is the function of the electrolyte in electrolysis?
faq.a: The electrolyte is the molten salt or solution that conducts electricity. It allows the ions to move between the electrodes.
asks: What is the liquid in the electrolysis cell?

faq.q: Is all metal extraction done by electrolysis?
faq.a: No, only the most reactive metals like sodium or aluminium usually require electrolysis. Less reactive metals can use displacement reactions.
asks: Do all metals need electricity to be extracted?
What is the easiest way to extract a metal?

facts: The reactivity series ranks metals by their tendency to lose electrons.
Displacement reactions occur when a more reactive metal reacts with a solution.
Electrolysis uses electrical energy to force non-spontaneous chemical reactions.
Aluminium is extracted from its ore using the process of electrolysis.

quiz.say: If you place magnesium metal into copper(ii) sulfate solution, what will happen?
quiz.why: Magnesium is more reactive than copper, so it will displace it.

wrong.0: This is incorrect because the reaction involves the metal, not just a color change.
wrong.2: This is tempting because the ions are in solution, but reactivity matters more.
wrong.3: This is wrong because copper is less reactive than magnesium.

quiz.say: What is the primary energy source for extracting sodium from its chloride salt?

options.show: Using a reactive metal like potassium.
options.say: Using a reactive metal like potassium.

options.show: Heating the salt to a high temperature.
options.say: Heating the salt to a high temperature.

quiz.why: Sodium is extremely reactive, so only a large input of electrical energy can force its extraction.

wrong.0: Potassium is also highly reactive, and the reaction would be too violent or complex.
wrong.2: Acids are not strong enough to overcome sodium's high reactivity.
wrong.3: Heat alone cannot break the strong bonds in the salt to release sodium.
